- **self**: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation (18/9)

## Structure and components

- [statement] Selection is part of fitting: repeat feature and parameter selection inside each training/validation split, then evaluate the selected pipeline on a later untouched test segment. Selecting once on all observations before assessing generalization biases the comparison. (medium confidence) — https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume11/cawley10a/cawley10a.pdf · keywords: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00060

## How it works

- [statement] Correlated indicators can have low individual permutation importance because the fitted model still accesses similar information through another feature. Inspect redundancy before interpreting a low ranking as lack of useful information; scikit-learn suggests clustering correlated features and retaining a representative, while Molnar distinguishes conditional importance as information unique to a feature. (medium confidence) — https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/permutation_importance.html · keywords: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation · also: https://christophm.github.io/interpretable-ml-book/feature-importance.html
- [statement] Evaluate model quality before interpreting importance, and compute importance on unseen data when asking about generalization. Importance describes the particular fitted model and evaluation metric, not an intrinsic universal ranking of indicators. (medium confidence) — https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/permutation_importance.html · keywords: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation · also: https://christophm.github.io/interpretable-ml-book/feature-importance.html

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Permutation importance and retraining-based ablation answer different questions: the former perturbs inputs to an already fitted model, while the latter removes a feature and retrains before comparing error. A permutation ranking alone therefore does not establish the incremental value of a retrained indicator combination. (medium confidence) — https://christophm.github.io/interpretable-ml-book/feature-importance.html · keywords: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation · also: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/permutation_importance.html
- [statement] Hsu and Kuan report that investor strategies combining trading rules can improve on simple rules and can generate significant profits from individually unprofitable rules in their historical equity-index study. This scopes any blanket claim that combining indicators cannot help; it does not demonstrate crypto-perpetual profitability. (low confidence) — https://homepage.ntu.edu.tw/~ckuan/pdf/snoop01.pdf · keywords: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation
- [statement] Technical-rule evidence can fail out of sample even after an in-sample data-snooping adjustment. Sullivan, Timmermann and White report historical benchmark outperformance after adjustment in their original sample but scant evidence of economic value in the subsequent sample. This historical equity-market result scopes confidence in combination searches; it does not measure crypto performance. (low confidence) — https://researchonline.lse.ac.uk/id/eprint/119144/1/dp303.pdf · keywords: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Methodological synthesis: for a baseline indicator set and each added or removed indicator family, rerun feature selection and tuning inside the same chronological outer training windows, then compare their held-out net results on the same outer test periods. This combines nested selection, retraining-based removal, chronological testing and cost-aware evaluation; it is a proposed evaluation design rather than a demonstrated SOL edge. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7776094/ · keywords: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation · also: https://christophm.github.io/interpretable-ml-book/feature-importance.html, https://github.com/remy-rm511/nasdaq-quant-ml-research/blob/main/README.md, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S266682702100030X
- [statement] Park and Irwin identify searching across optimization periods, trading systems and trading assumptions on the same data as data snooping. Methodological implication: an indicator-combination ablation is also a search over models, so selection must remain inside training and validation rather than repeatedly choosing the best outer-test result. (medium confidence) — https://ageconsearch.umn.edu/record/14771/files/rr050004.pdf · keywords: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7776094/
- [statement] The FX study titled “FX technical trading rules can be profitable sometimes!” reports short-period out-of-sample profitability after addressing costs and data snooping, but says the rules are not consistently profitable. Its result supports testing temporal persistence rather than treating one successful held-out period as a universal property of an indicator combination. (low confidence) — https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1057521916301958 · keywords: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation
- [statement] For nested ablation, compare a baseline, its indicator-augmented version, and further feature-group additions under the same model, execution rule and chronological evaluation. Judge the incremental result on held-out net trading performance rather than predictive accuracy alone. This is a methodological synthesis, not evidence of a profitable SOL combination. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00060 · keywords: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation · also: https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume11/cawley10a/cawley10a.pdf
- [statement] The Bitcoin paper explicitly describes its selector comparison as a validation heuristic rather than a fully nested optimization: the same validation segment supports hyperparameter search and comparison of selectors. It reserves substantive conclusions for untouched test returns. Use this paper as a controlled comparison example, not as proof that a completely nested selection procedure was implemented. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00060 · keywords: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Nested validation separates feature and parameter selection in inner training folds from performance estimation in outer test folds. The cited bioinformatics methodology establishes this separation for independent data; it does not by itself establish a suitable time-series split for crypto. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7776094/ · keywords: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation
- [statement] Molnar explains that permutation importance includes interaction effects and can count the same interaction in both participating features. Individual importance values therefore need not add up to the total performance drop; combination tests should not infer joint value by summing single-feature rankings. (low confidence) — https://christophm.github.io/interpretable-ml-book/feature-importance.html · keywords: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation
- [statement] Peng and coauthors studied stock-direction prediction using selected technical indicators and neural networks. Their trading experiments did not significantly outperform buy-and-hold despite apparently useful out-of-sample classification results. This is a scoped counterexample to treating predictive accuracy as evidence of economic superiority. (low confidence) — https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S266682702100030X · keywords: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation
- [statement] In the Bitcoin study, net returns subtract transaction costs proportional to position turnover. Its cost assumption proxies execution frictions; the backtest does not simulate depth, partial fills, routing or changing spreads. Treat its feature-combination results as conditional on that execution model. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00060 · keywords: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation
- [statement] The Bitcoin study reports that technical indicators improve some selected configurations, while adding EGARCH features beyond technical indicators does not deliver a statistically reliable improvement. This is a study-specific result, not a generic ranking or a demonstrated SOL/Jupiter edge. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00060 · keywords: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation
- [statement] A fixed execution threshold does not fully isolate predictive information: richer features can change forecast magnitudes and therefore how often trades pass the threshold. Report trade frequency alongside net results and distinguish predictive improvement from changes in execution activity. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00060 · keywords: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation
- [statement] For the incremental comparison, use aligned out-of-sample return differences and dependence-aware uncertainty estimates, and account for the family of combinations searched. This recommendation combines the Bitcoin study’s paired block-bootstrap comparisons with research showing why inference on only the surviving best trading rule is misleading. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00060 · keywords: Incremental net value of indicator combinations through nested ablation · also: https://researchonline.lse.ac.uk/id/eprint/119144/1/dp303.pdf
